children: JSW Energy plans to raise around Rs 1,500 crore, while JSW Steel could raise Rs 1,350 crore through shorter-tenor bonds
Two JSW Group companies, JSW Energy and JSW Steel, are planning to raise a combined Rs 2,850 crore through shorter-tenor bonds in the October-December quarter, according to two bankers.

JSW Energy is looking to raise around Rs 1,500 crore through bonds with a tenor of up to five years, while JSW Steel could raise around Rs 1,350 crore through three-year or four-year debt, the bankers said, requesting anonymity as they are not authorised to speak to the media.
The companies could tap the bond market in October if market interest rates are favourable, according to the bankers. JSW Energy and JSW Steel did not respond to emails seeking comment.
JSW Energy's bonds are rated AA by India Ratings. The company has around Rs 2,500 crore of outstanding bonds.

The company, which has thermal, hydro and renewable power operations, last raised Rs 800 crore through three-year and five-year bonds in March 2025. The bonds carried interest rates of 8.75 per cent and 8.80 per cent, respectively.

An AA rating indicates a high degree of safety regarding timely servicing of financial obligations, although it also indicates that the instruments carry a higher degree of credit risk than those with higher ratings.
JSW Steel has an AA+ rating from Icra and India Ratings, with more than Rs 6,100 crore of outstanding bonds.
The steelmaker last tapped the bond market more than two years ago, raising Rs 2,250 crore through five-year and seven-year bonds at interest rates of 8.35 per cent and 8.43 per cent, respectively.
The proposed issuances would add to the companies' existing bond liabilities if completed.
